prompt: The console hides the clinical-notes link from receptionists. What does that protect?

choices.text: The notes, from every receptionist who uses the console
choices.why: The address still answers whoever asks it.

choices.text: Nothing: hiding it is design, not access control
choices.why: Right. A better screen, and no barrier.

choices.text: The notes from scripts, but not from browsers
choices.why: Neither: both send requests directly.

choices.text: The session cookie
choices.why: Hiding a link has nothing to do with the cookie.

prompt: Which of these are claims the client makes, not facts the server knows? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a hidden form field role=physio
choices.why: Edited in two clicks.

choices.text: a cookie is_admin=1
choices.why: The client stores and sends it.

choices.text: a parameter ?role=admin in the address
choices.why: Typed by whoever sends the request.

choices.text: bruno's role in the server's STAFF table
choices.why: That is the fact the check reads.

prompt: Put the three rules of the lesson in the order it gives them.
items: check on the server, on every request
take the role from the server

prompt: Where did OWASP's Top 10 of 2021 place broken access control?

choices.text: Third, behind injection and cryptographic failures
choices.why: Injection fell to third that year.

choices.text: First
choices.why: Right, and it stayed first in 2025.

choices.text: Tenth
choices.why: It was at the top.

choices.text: It was not on the list that year
choices.why: It led the list.

prompt: How many of the six tests failed against the first version of the console?
Why does the test `test_the_console_hides_notes_from_a_receptionist` pass against the flawed version?

choices.text: The test is wrong and should fail
choices.why: It is right: the link is hidden.

choices.text: Flask caches the page for receptionists
choices.why: No cache is involved.

choices.text: The page does hide the link; hiding was never the flaw
choices.why: Right. It sits beside the failing test to show hiding and control are different things.

choices.text: bruno is not signed in during that test
choices.why: sign_in writes his name into the session.

prompt: What did `curl -si http://127.0.0.1:5000/export` return against the first version?

choices.text: 401, because nobody was signed in
choices.why: That is what the fixed version returns.

choices.text: 200 OK and the CSV of patients
choices.why: Right. The route never asked who was there.

choices.text: 403, because curl has no role
choices.why: Nothing was checked at all.

choices.text: A redirect to the sign-in page of the console
choices.why: There was no redirect.

prompt: Where does `requires` take the person's role from?

choices.text: From the hidden field of the form
choices.why: That was the flaw it replaces.

choices.text: From a role stored in the session cookie
choices.why: The session carries only the name.

choices.text: From STAFF, the server's own table
choices.why: Right. The request says who; the server says what they may do.

choices.text: From the route's address
choices.why: The address names the patient, not the role.

prompt: Match each answer of `requires` to its case.

pairs.right: nobody signed in, or a name the server does not know

prompt: Why was the hidden `role` field removed from the page, though nothing reads it any more?

choices.text: A field nobody reads is one somebody starts reading again
choices.why: Right. Leaving it invites the old mistake back.

choices.text: Browsers refuse forms with hidden fields
choices.why: They accept them.

choices.text: It made the page slow to load
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: The test checks that the page has no hidden fields
choices.why: No test looks for it.

prompt: The decorator keeps the view's name, which Flask uses to tell routes apart, with `@___(view)`.
After the first fix, how many tests still failed?
What does `test_every_route_says_who_may_use_it` check?

choices.text: That every route returns 401 to an anonymous request
choices.why: It sends no request at all.

choices.text: That the admin may open every route
choices.why: The admin may not read notes, by design.

choices.text: That each route's view carries allowed_roles
choices.why: Right. A route that has not declared who may use it fails the build.

choices.text: That routes are listed in alphabetical order
choices.why: Order is irrelevant.

prompt: Which routes did the test name after the first fix? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: /console
choices.why: Open to any signed-in staff, with nothing saying which.

choices.text: /agenda
choices.why: The same.

choices.text: /export
choices.why: The leak.

choices.text: /patients/<name>/notes
choices.why: The first fix decorated it.

prompt: Why can ana, the administrator, not read clinical notes?

choices.text: The decorator has a bug for admins
choices.why: It does what the route declares.

choices.text: Admins are expected to use the export instead
choices.why: The export counts notes; it does not show them.

choices.text: Flask forbids one person holding two roles
choices.why: Flask knows nothing of roles.

choices.text: Least privilege: her work needs none
choices.why: Right. Admin implying everything gives the most-attacked account the most data.

prompt: After the second fix, what did the same curl request to /export return?

choices.text: 200, empty CSV
choices.why: The view never ran.

choices.text: 401 UNAUTHORIZED
choices.why: Right. No session, so requires stopped it.

choices.text: 403 FORBIDDEN, because curl is not an admin
choices.why: With no session at all the answer is 401.

choices.text: 404 NOT FOUND, because the route was removed from the console
choices.why: The route still exists.

prompt: The test lists every route Flask knows with `app.url_map.___()`.
carla may read clinical notes. What does the role check not answer?

choices.text: Which patients' notes she reads
choices.why: Right. Ownership is the other half, lesson 13.

choices.text: Whether she is signed in to the console
choices.why: requires checks that first.

choices.text: Whether she is a physiotherapist
choices.why: That is exactly what it answers.

choices.text: Whether the route exists
choices.why: Flask answers that.

prompt: The notes route is locked, and the console's search quotes the first line of every note. What does the lesson call that?

choices.text: A role hierarchy
choices.why: Not about roles above or below.

choices.text: Session fixation
choices.why: That is lesson 10.

choices.text: Data leaking out of the side door
choices.why: Right. Every way to the same data needs the same check.

choices.text: Deny by default
choices.why: That is the defence, not the flaw.

prompt: Which habits apply to a route that grants roles? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: record who made the change
choices.why: In a log nobody can edit.

choices.text: end the sessions it affects
choices.why: A removed role takes effect now.

choices.text: refuse granting a role to yourself
choices.why: A second person approves.

choices.text: hide its link from the page
choices.why: Fine as design, and protects nothing.

prompt: A new route `/patients/<name>/summary` shows each patient's last note, and the developer forgot `@requires`. What happens?

choices.text: Flask refuses to start the application
choices.why: Flask has no opinion about roles.

choices.text: The route test fails, and names the route
choices.why: Right. Deny by default, held by a test.

choices.text: Nothing, until somebody reports a leak
choices.why: That was the world before the test.

choices.text: The decorator applies itself automatically
choices.why: Decorators apply only where written.

prompt: A mobile app sends `X-Role: physio` with each request, and the server checks that header. What is wrong?

choices.text: Headers are encrypted, so the server cannot read them
choices.why: It reads them fine.

choices.text: Nothing, if the app is published in the official stores
choices.why: Any program can send the same header.

choices.text: The role is a claim the sender makes
choices.why: Right. Take the identity from the session, and the role from the server.

choices.text: The header name should start with lower case
choices.why: Header names are case-insensitive.
